reuse.why: Builds getExpectedAmount in shared/schedules.ts on the existing getApproxNumberThreshold and routes the existing getScheduledAmount's range branch through getRangeAmount, though getScheduledAmount itself stays a separate entry point.

duplication.why: Removes five inline midpoint copies in favour of one helper; the remaining overlap is getScheduledAmount, which keeps its own number/range dispatch next to getExpectedAmount.

placement.why: The amount rule lives in shared/schedules.ts beside the other schedule helpers, and the API model, template, forecast, schedules app and preview code only call it.

scope.why: Changes stay on schedule amounts, but several comments rewritten in step 3 ('furthest-from-zero end') are left stale after step 4 changes the rule.

maintainability.why: Server paths share one function, but two exported helpers (getExpectedAmount with the approximate rule, getScheduledAmount without it, used by the client Balance and lists) now encode overlapping rules that can drift, and comments describe an outdated rule.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Client callers of getScheduledAmount (Balance.tsx, SchedulesTable.tsx, mobile lists) bypass getExpectedAmount, so the approximate-amount rule is not applied there.

disguised_duplication.where: getScheduledAmount keeps its own type dispatch, but the range arithmetic is shared through getRangeAmount rather than re-written.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedAmount gains the op parameter and an 'isapprox' branch; getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts remains a parallel definition that handles ranges via getRangeAmount but not the approximate rule.
